response: Ward E (Byculla, Agripada, Mumbai Central) billed Rs 6,322,991 against a road repair budget of Rs 5,300,000, using 119.3% of budget. Of 118 jobs, 30.5% reopened within 30 days and 62.7% met their deadline. Conditions matter here: the city had 18 days of heavy or worse rain, and this low-lying ward (index 0.7) floods often. Still, Rs 2,496,332 was billed on DLP roads. DLP means the road is still under the original contractor's warranty, so repairs should cost the city nothing. This spending needs review. Also, 9 jobs were priced more than 30% above the rate card and should be checked. The top contractor by spend was Western Coast Asphalt Co (synthetic). Example work orders are WO25-00528 and WO25-00985. Ask the ward office whether WO25-00528 was on a DLP road and, if so, why the city paid for it.
